controls.title: Information security during disruption
controls.description: The entity shall plan how to maintain information security at an appropriate level during disruption.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall plan how to maintain information security at an appropriate level during disruption.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall implement and maintain:
1) information security controls, supporting systems, and tools within business continuity and ICT continuity plans.
2) processes to maintain existing information security controls during disruption.
3) compensating controls for information security controls that cannot be maintained during disruption.
controls.domain: T9 Information Systems Continuity Management
controls.category: T9.1 ICT readiness for business continuity
assessment_criteria: The entity shall implement and maintain: information security controls, supporting systems, and tools within business continuity and ICT continuity plans.
The entity shall implement and maintain: processes to maintain existing information security controls during disruption.
The entity shall implement and maintain: compensating controls for information security controls that cannot be maintained during disruption.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Based on risk assessment. Implementation priority: P3. Control type: Preventive, Corrective. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T9.2.2.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.29; NIST SP 800-53 r5: CP-2, CP-6, CP-7; ISRv3: 7.3.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
The entity should determine its requirements for adapting information security controls during disruption. Information security requirements should be included in the business continuity management processes.
Plans should be developed, implemented, tested, reviewed, and evaluated to maintain or restore the security of information of critical business processes following interruption or failure. Security of information should be restored at the required level and in the required time frames.
In the context of business continuity and ICT continuity planning, it can be necessary to adapt the information security requirements depending on the type of disruption, compared to normal operational conditions. As part of the business impact analysis and risk assessment performed within business continuity management, the consequences of loss of confidentiality and integrity of information should be considered and prioritized in addition to the need for maintaining availability.

controls.title: Testing, Maintaining and Re-Assessing Information Systems Continuity Plans
controls.description: The entity shall test, maintain and re-assess its information systems continuity plans.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall test, maintain and re-assess its information systems continuity plans.

Sub-Controls:
The entity shall:
1) periodically test the continuity plan for the information systems following the established procedures to determine the effectiveness of the plan and the organizational readiness to execute the plan.
2) establish lessons learned and update the information systems continuity plans to ensure they are always up to date.
controls.domain: T9 Information Systems Continuity Management
controls.category: T9.2 Testing, Maintaining and Reassessing Plans
assessment_criteria: The entity shall: periodically test the continuity plan for the information systems following the established procedures to determine the effectiveness of the plan and the organizational readiness to execute the plan.
The entity shall: establish lessons learned and update the information systems continuity plans to ensure they are always up to date.
controls.ai_notes:
Applicability: Based on risk assessment. Implementation priority: P3. Control type: Preventive. UAE IA v1.1 (Annex G): T9.3.1.
Mapping to leading standards (Annex D). ISO/IEC 27001:2022: none listed; ISO/IEC 27002:2022: 5.3; NIST SP 800-53 r5: CP-4; ISRv3: 7.5.
Implementation Guidance (for information purposes only; not a requirement of the standard):
Business continuity plan tests should ensure that all members of the recovery team and other relevant staff are aware of the plans and their responsibility for business continuity and information security and know their role when a plan is invoked.
The test schedule for business continuity plan(s) should indicate how and when each element of the plan should be tested. Each element of the plan(s) should be tested frequently.
A variety of techniques should be used in order to provide assurance that the plan(s) will operate in real life. These should include:
a. table-top testing of various scenarios (discussing the business recovery arrangements using example interruptions).
b. simulations (particularly for training people in their post-incident/crisis management roles).
c. technical recovery testing (ensuring information systems can be restored effectively).
d. testing recovery at an alternate site (running business processes in parallel with recovery operations away from the main site).
e. tests of supplier facilities and services (ensuring externally provided services and products will meet the contracted commitment).
f. complete rehearsals (testing that the entity, personnel, equipment, facilities, and processes can cope with interruptions).
These techniques can be used by any entity. They should be applied in a way that is relevant to the specific recovery plan. The results of tests should be recorded, and actions taken to improve the plans, where necessary.
Responsibility should be assigned for regular reviews of each business continuity plan. The identification of changes in business arrangements not yet reflected in the business continuity plans should be followed by an appropriate update of the plan. This formal change control process should ensure that the updated plans are distributed and reinforced by regular reviews of the complete plan.
Examples of changes where updating of business continuity plans should be considered are acquisition of new equipment, upgrading of systems and changes in:
a. personnel.
b. addresses or telephone numbers.
c. business strategy.
d. location, facilities, and resources.
e. legislation.
f. contractors, suppliers, and key customers.
g. processes, or new or withdrawn ones.
h. risk (operational and financial).

controls.title: Governance Framework
controls.description: The entity shall establish, implement, and regularly review a cloud security policy that addresses key aspects of cloud security.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall establish, implement, and regularly review a cloud security policy that addresses key aspects of cloud security. When defining the information security policy for cloud computing, the cloud service customer shall take the following into account:
• information stored in the cloud computing environment can be subject to access and management by the cloud service provider.
• assets can be maintained in the cloud computing environment, e.g. application programs.
• processes can run on a multi-tenant, virtualized cloud service.
• the cloud service users and the context in which they use the cloud service.
• the cloud service administrators of the cloud service customer who have privileged access.
• the geographical locations of the cloud service provider's organization and the countries where the cloud service provider can store the cloud service customer data (even temporarily).

controls.title: Data Governance
controls.description: The entity shall implement policies and procedures for data classification, labelling and handling throughout its’ lifecycle to secure the data that is resident (permanently or temporarily) within the service’s geographically distributed (physical and virtual) applications, infrastructure, network and systems components and shared with other third parties to ascertain any regulatory, statutory, or supply chain agreement (SLA) compliance impact.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall implement policies and procedures for data classification, labelling and handling throughout its’ lifecycle to secure the data that is resident (permanently or temporarily) within the service’s geographically distributed (physical and virtual) applications, infrastructure, network and systems components and shared with other third parties to ascertain any regulatory, statutory, or supply chain agreement (SLA) compliance impact.

The entity shall classify their data before migrating to the cloud, based on the potential impact of its compromise on operations, reputation, financial stability, and regulatory compliance and align this classification with the levels outlined in the National Cloud Security Policy.

controls.title: Encryption and Cryptography
controls.description: The entity shall establish and implement policies and procedures for the use of encryption protocols for the protection of sensitive data in storage and data in transmission as per applicable legal, statutory, and regulatory compliance obligations.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall establish and implement policies and procedures for the use of encryption protocols for the protection of sensitive data in storage and data in transmission as per applicable legal, statutory, and regulatory compliance obligations.

The entity shall ensure secure key management practices are implemented.

Partial Sovereign Cloud Requirements
Consumers shall conduct a risk assessment to determine whether Hold Your Own Key (HYOK) capabilities are required to be implemented. If the risk assessment indicates that HYOK is necessary, consumers shall implement it to retain exclusive control over encryption keys and mitigate the risk of unauthorized access to data. In cases where HYOK is implemented, consumers shall ensure that key access, revocation, and auditability are supported without dependency on the CSP.

The entity shall ensure that data classified above Confidential/Restricted are strictly stored and processed in Sovereign Cloud environment.

controls.title: Infrastructure & Application Security
controls.description: The entity shall implement and maintain effective measures to ensure the secure design, configuration, and operation of AI/ML infrastructure and applications throughout their lifecycle, including:
controls.full_text:
The entity shall implement and maintain effective measures to ensure the secure design, configuration, and operation of AI/ML infrastructure and applications throughout their lifecycle, including:
• Maintaining an up-to-date inventory of AI/ML assets and applying cyber security controls appropriate to their sensitivity, criticality, and value.
• Ensuring AI/ML systems are securely configured in line with approved security baselines and configuration standards.
• Identifying, testing, and applying patches and updates in a timely manner to maintain system integrity and resilience.
• Implementing a systematic vulnerability management process to detect, assess, and remediate weaknesses in AI/ML systems.

controls.full_text:
The entity shall establish and maintain controls to ensure the secure design, development, and protection of AI/ML algorithms and models throughout their lifecycle, including:
• Integrating cyber security considerations into the design and development of AI/ML models from the earliest stages to proactively mitigate risks and avoid retrofitting controls post-deployment.
• Implementing security measures to protect AI/ML models from threats that could compromise their integrity, confidentiality, or availability.
• Ensuring the security of AI/ML inference processes by safeguarding inference data and maintaining its integrity and confidentiality.
• Enforcing robust access controls over AI/ML training data to preserve confidentiality, integrity, privacy, and auditability.
• Applying stringent data protection controls for AI/ML data both at rest and in motion to ensure its confidentiality and integrity.

controls.description: The entity shall implement and maintain operational controls to ensure the resilience, reliability, and secure functioning of AI/ML systems, including:
controls.full_text:
The entity shall implement and maintain operational controls to ensure the resilience, reliability, and secure functioning of AI/ML systems, including:
• Tailoring cyber security measures to the specific application domains of AI/ML systems.
• Incorporation of redundancy, failover mechanisms, and other measures to maintain availability during disruptions.
• Integrating AI/ML systems into business continuity and disaster recovery planning, with regular testing of restoration capabilities and continuity scenarios.
• Conducting comprehensive security testing and validation to verify the security and resilience of AI/ML systems against potential threats.

• IoT security, availability, and privacy requirements in line with all applicable standards, laws, and regulations.

The entity shall ensure third party access to IoT devices:
• are granted based on the least privileged principle.
• are granted for a limited timeframe.
• are reviewed periodically.

controls.title: Data Privacy and Governance
controls.description: The entity shall: identify and classify data collected throughout the IoT ecosystem.
controls.full_text:
The entity shall:
• identify and classify data collected throughout the IoT ecosystem.
• ensure, through contracts, that they are provided with clear and transparent information about how their data is being used, by whom, and for what purposes for each IoT device and service.
• ensure, through contracts, that it can exercise its rights to information, access, erasure, rectification, data portability, restriction of processing, objection to processing, and its right not to be evaluated based on automated processing; and
• protect the confidentiality, integrity, and/or availability of data, including personally identifiable information (PII), collected by, stored on, processed by, or transmitted to or from the IoT device.

The entity shall ensure that contractual requirements with cloud service providers (CSPs) are formalized and agreed upon, including:
• Non-disclosure agreements.
• Service level agreements.
• Security and privacy requirements.
• Sovereignty requirements.
• Availability requirements.
• Incident reporting requirements.
• service exit requirements.
• change management requirements.
• right to audit.

Entity shall:
• avoid the collection of sensitive data.
• minimize the data collected and retained.
• restrict access to the physical and logical location of data only to authorized individuals

controls.title: Secure and trusted communications
controls.description: The entity shall implement secure sessions ensuring:
controls.full_text:
The entity shall implement secure sessions ensuring:
• active sessions are unique and cannot be shared or predicted.
• non-essential sessions are timed out and invalidated.
• session tokens are unique with a minimum level of entropy.
• sessions are expired after fixed time of inactivity

The entity shall ensure that communication protocols employ encrypted channels, integrity protection, and authenticated connections to share information between IoT systems. Proven encryption techniques shall be used to protect data within all IoT systems and their underlying infrastructure.

controls.title: Access Control
controls.description: Entity shall implement identity and access management controls to :
controls.full_text:
Entity shall implement identity and access management controls to :
• enforce least privilege with unique identification and accountability for access to IoT resources.
• implement strong authentication mechanisms, including multi-factor authentication, for all IoT systems.
• manage access throughout the resource lifecycle, ensuring secure storage of credentials and prohibiting hard-coded credentials.
• conduct regular access reviews to verify permissions and implement compensating controls as needed.
• align password policies with complexity standards, requiring periodic updates.

controls.title: Application Security
controls.description: IoT solution components such as applications, middleware, APIs, and devices shall be configured for secure authentication and information exchange over encrypted channels.
controls.full_text:
IoT solution components such as applications, middleware, APIs, and devices shall be configured for secure authentication and information exchange over encrypted channels.

Entity shall ensure that applications are implemented with end-to-end security controls and availability aspects across the IoT solution and shall enforce access control rules on the trusted service layer.

Entity shall utilize a secure and dedicated gateway for data normalization and processing within IoT networks.

controls.title: Device Security
controls.description: Entity shall ensure that: IoT devices and sensors are securely installed and configured to prevent unauthorized access.
controls.full_text:
Entity shall ensure that:
• IoT devices and sensors are securely installed and configured to prevent unauthorized access.
• IoT devices are managed remotely over encrypted channels with security logs enabled.
• A documented device management strategy is in place for periodic updates and maintenance.
• Security patches from authentic sources are applied securely and tested for compatibility.
• All updates are assessed for risk and impact before deployment.
• Compensatory measures are applied for devices at end-of-life.

controls.title: Network Management
controls.description: Entity shall ensure IoT networks are secured by:
controls.full_text:
Entity shall ensure IoT networks are secured by:
• utilizing secure ports and protocols with authentication and encryption enabled.
• considering security controls and interoperability across different routing networks.
• segregating IoT networks from the corporate network and implementing micro-segmentation for controlled access.
• restricting and controlling information exchange and infrastructure management of IoT devices and applications.
• disabling unused and default network services, protocols, and ports.
• conducting IoT solution administration and management via a separate, segregated network.
• employing best practice cryptography for secure communications in consumer IoT devices.

controls.title: Audit Logging
controls.description: The entity shall produce, store, protect, and analyze logs for IoT devices, systems, and applications for events such as:
controls.full_text:
The entity shall produce, store, protect, and analyze logs for IoT devices, systems, and applications for events such as:
• User logins, logouts, and unsuccessful authentication attempts.
• Connection and disconnection attempts, including unsuccessful connection attempts.
• Unsuccessful authorization attempts.
• Access to sensitive data.
• Importing and exporting data from removable media.
• Any changes in access privileges.
• Creation, modification, and deletion of data by users.
• Impactful operations.
• Remote operations.
• Security update failures.
• Physical access attempts, where possible.
• Emergency access attempts, where possible.
